symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions on leaf blades
Lesions have greyish-white centers with dark brown borders
Severe lesions coalesce, causing complete blighting of leaves
Neck rot: brown/black ring at panicle base causing empty chalky grains
favorable_conditions: High relative humidity (> 90%), prolonged leaf wetness, cloudy skies, and excessive nitrogen application.
prevention: Use certified resistant seed varieties.
Avoid excessive top-dressing with nitrogenous fertilizers.
Seed treatment with Tricyclazole (2g/kg seed).
Ensure proper plant spacing for canopy aeration.
treatment: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/liter of water.
Or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/liter.
Or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1 ml/liter.
Repeat spray after 10-12 days if disease pressure persists.

symptoms: Linear stripes of bright yellow powdery pustules (uredinia) on leaves
Chlorotic stripes running parallel to leaf veins
Pustules rupture releasing masses of yellow airborne spores
Yellow powder stains fingers or cloth when brushed against leaf
favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (10-18°C), free moisture from dew or light fog, susceptible cultivars.
prevention: Grow rust-resistant cultivars (e.g. PBW-725, DBW-187, DBW-303).
Timely sowing before mid-November in rust-prone zones.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer.
treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1.0 ml/liter of water.
Or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.2 ml/liter of water.
Spray uniformly covering the entire foliage upon detecting initial isolated foci.

symptoms: Dark brown to black circular spots with characteristic concentric rings (target-board effect)
Yellow halo surrounding the concentric leaf lesions
Infection begins on oldest lower leaves and progresses upwards
Collar rot on stems and dark sunken leathery lesions on stem-end of fruit
favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) accompanied by heavy dew, rain, or frequent overhead irrigation.
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Mulch soil around plants to prevent splash dispersal of soil spores.
Prune lower leaves that touch the soil.
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers.
treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/liter as prophylactic.
For active infection: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/liter or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/liter.
Bio-control: Trichoderma harzianum soil and foliar drench.

symptoms: Severe upward curling and puckering of leaves
Stunted bushy plant growth with shortened internodes
Interveinal chlorosis and thick leathery leaf texture
Flower abortion and failure of fruit set
favorable_conditions: High whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) population during warm, dry weather.
prevention: Raise nursery seedlings under 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets.
Install yellow sticky traps @ 15 traps/acre.
Grow barrier crops like 2-3 border rows of Maize or Sorghum.
Plant ToLCV-tolerant hybrid varieties.
treatment: Direct viral cure is not possible; manage whitefly vector promptly.
Spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/liter or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/liter.
Spray Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2 ml/liter as deterrent.
Uproot and burn severely infected individual plants.

disease_name: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
symptoms: Water-soaked angular spots bounded by veinlets on leaves
Lesions turn reddish-brown to dark black
Black arm symptom: elongated dark cankers on stems causing breakage
Water-soaked oily spots on cotton bolls resulting in boll rot
favorable_conditions: Warm humid climate (28-32°C, relative humidity > 80%) with driving rain or overhead sprinkler irrigation.
prevention: Acid delinting of cotton seeds with concentrated sulfuric acid.
Seed treatment with Streptocycline (100 ppm) + Copper Oxychloride (2g/kg).
Destruction of infected crop residues after harvest.
treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/liter.
Or Copper Hydroxide 53.8% DF @ 2 g/liter.
Avoid irrigation during peak disease intensity.

symptoms: Vibrant green, uniform leaf color without chlorosis or necrosis
Intact leaf lamina with no spots, lesions, or wilting
Strong turgidity and healthy vascular system
Normal physiological growth appropriate for current stage
favorable_conditions: Balanced soil fertility, adequate sunlight, and optimal moisture management.
prevention: Maintain balanced NPK fertigation according to soil test.
Regular scouting for early pest appearance.
Good drainage to prevent waterlogging.
treatment: No chemical fungicides or bactericides required.
Continue standard agronomic care and balanced nutrition.

disease_name: Aphids & Sucking Pest Complex (Aphis gossypii / Myzus persicae)
symptoms: Colonies of small green/black pear-shaped aphids clustered along the midrib and leaf margins
Curling, crinkling, and cupping of terminal leaves with stunted vegetative growth
Sticky glistening honeydew excretion covering leaf surface attracting black sooty mold (Capnodium spp.)
Vectoring of viral pathogens across tender shoots and leaf veins
favorable_conditions: Cloudy, humid weather with mild temperatures (18-28°C), dry spells after rains, and excess vegetative lushness from surplus nitrogen application.
prevention: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) to monitor and mass-trap winged aphids.
Conserve natural biological predators: Ladybird beetles (Coccinellids), hoverfly larvae (Syrphids), and green lacewings (Chrysoperla carnea).
Avoid excessive top-dressing with nitrogenous fertilizers which stimulate succulent vegetative growth.
Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Azadirachtin 10,000 ppm @ 2 ml/liter as prophylactic barrier.
treatment: Bio-pesticide: Spray Verticillium lecanii or Beauveria bassiana @ 5 g/liter at evening hours under high humidity.
Chemical Control: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/liter or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2 g/liter.
Alternative Systemic: Flonicamid 50% WG @ 0.3 g/liter or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.25 g/liter.
Ensure thorough spray coverage targeting the undersides of foliage.
